method: Post-inference visual correspondence review against original photos and the pre-inference reference rectangles. A correspondence identifies which visible object a prediction describes, not whether its name was identified. Predictions/results remain unchanged.

observations: lm_1 correctly names and encloses Canton Tower.
lm_2 encloses the visible CTF/East Tower, but its primary name is generic and candidates mix CTF and IFC; this is ambiguous identity, not two recognized towers.
No separate prediction encloses the real IFC/West Tower to the left of CTF; IFC is missed even though its name occurs in lm_2 candidates.

lm_3 center and box cover the central river island; if the target includes the stadium structure described in evidence, tall masts above y=0.61 are not fully covered. Candidate Haixinsha Island is outside the fixed identity scoring scope.
lm_4 approximately encloses the far-right building bearing CCB signage; no unverified proper identity is assigned.

All six output horizontal pair orders agree visually. The five emitted vertical pair-axis relations agree with approximate visible centers; lm_1/lm_2 has a 0.03 center gap and correctly has no vertical relation. These center orders do not assert whole-object non-overlap or depth. Only fixed reference target pairs enter scored geometry results.
lm_1 box encloses China Zun with a generic primary description and a correct but uncertain CITIC Tower (China Zun) candidate.

lm_2 box encloses CCTV Headquarters with a generic primary description and correct but uncertain CCTV Headquarters candidate. Its projected center lies in the bounding rectangle and can fall on foreground occlusion rather than a visible facade pixel.
lm_7 box encloses Parkview Green's glass pyramid envelope accurately, but no proper-name candidate is given.

lm_3, lm_4, lm_5, lm_6 boxes and centers correspond approximately to the visible FFC-signed, rightmost tapered, lattice-crowned and far-left dark towers. These additional identities are not independently scored.
All five fixed pair-axis relations can be visually checked and are correctly emitted; no arbitrary geographic direction or depth follows from them.
Correct Oriental Pearl Tower identity; bbox encloses spire, spheres, shaft and major support legs with small boundary differences.
Reported center (0.5,0.5) is visibly on the shaft but is not the exact rectangle midpoint (0.56,0.485); this is an approximate model measurement, not a deterministic conversion error.
Only one extracted target, so an empty relation list is appropriate.
